messages:
anna_keller: Heads up — procurement sim flagged a weird thing: cheap spot GPUs in eu-west are increasingly expensive once you factor cross-region egress and intermittent inter-AZ network throttling when we spill. Thinking we should add egress-aware scoring to the bidder, not just price vs capacity. Anyone seen this in prod?

mike_chan: Yup. We saw a similar spike last Tuesday. grafana shows retransmits + p95 token latency climb when hosts come from hotspot AZs. Link: https://grafana.redwood/procure/d/7Ff/procure-metrics

jess_rodriguez: Can you paste the numbers? Egress is per-GB and for batch/embeddings that kills unit economics fast.

anna_keller: Quick numbers: cheap-pool price 0.18/hr but adds ~0.05/GB egress effective when we spill to other regions; for our embed-heavy workload that's ~0.02 extra per unit. If preempt_prob is high we also pay migration penalty.

theo_ops: We already compute preempt probability per pool. Question: where do we calculate the combined score — bidder service or orchestrator?

anna_keller: Prefer bidder (procurement) so decision uses real-time pool metrics. Proposed score: effective_cost = spot_price + (egress_est * egress_price) + (preempt_prob * migration_penalty). Then rank by lowest effective_cost but with a capacity floor.

mike_chan: Watch out — capacity-optimized pools sometimes have lower preempt but also lower NIC throughput (observed throttling), so p99 latency can still worsen.

jess_rodriguez: Maybe we do egress buckets (high/med/low) and treat high as a hard penalty. Thresholding is simpler than trying to tune weights live.

anna_keller: Prototype config snippet I used in the sim:

```json
{
  "bid_strategy": "region_aware",
  "score_weights": {"price": 0.6, "preempt_prob": 0.2, "egress_est": 0.2},
  "egress_cost_table": {"eu-west-1": "0.09", "eu-west-2": "0.085", "us-west-2": "0.045"},
  "migration_penalty_secs": "120"
}
```

mike_chan: Can we simulate this end-to-end? I'll run procure-sim with our embed-heavy profile and the new scoring. Command I'm using: `./tools/procure-sim --profile embed-heavy --strategy region_aware --duration 24h --out sims/2312345678.csv`

anna_keller: Early sim results: region_aware reduces avg unit-cost ~8% in eu-west and p99 token latency down ~15%, but capacity utilization drops ~6% (we left cheaper nodes unused).

jess_rodriguez: :thinking_face: Sounds like a tradeoff. We should pilot for 12h against production traffic and check SLOs.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: procurement/bidder v2 -> 2% hosts (2024-11-03T09:12:00Z) :rocket: 

mike_chan: Ack. Rollout plan: canary 2% -> 10% -> 50% with an automatic rollback trigger if unit-cost increases >3% OR p99 latency increases >5%. I'll add checks to the rollout job.

anna_keller: I'll open a PR with the new bidder scoring and add the egress columns to procurement dashboard. Also adding a quick toggle so we can switch to pure price-mode if needed.

jess_rodriguez: Assigning: @mike_chan for sims and rollout, @anna_keller for code + dashboard, @theo_ops for runbook updates.

theo_ops: Noted. Updating runbook: include steps to forcibly rebind KV cache, force-evict misbehaving hosts, and warm new hosts before routing traffic. Also adding a network-throttle detection play called "egress-spill-detect".

mike_chan: One more operational guard: cap max bid in regions historically hit by egress spikes so procurement cannot overspend during sudden spill events.

anna_keller: Agreed. We'll include historical egress volatility in our pool metadata and set soft-bid ceilings per-region. Putting this on the eng-sync agenda for tomorrow.

jess_rodriguez: Sounds good. Thanks all — let's watch the canary and review sims tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
